leads.work: Flow at meters with no deal: schedulers (Mary Poorman, Aimee Lannou, Jackie Young, Susan Hadix, Thu Nguyen) email Daren Farmer one at a time to ask him to extend an expired deal or create a new one, or else to send the gas to the Strangers contract, so they can clear allocation exceptions
leads.why: Many separate requests in a few weeks, each for one meter and a few days of small volumes. The usual cause is valves not shut by 9am or meters shut in late. It often takes several rounds of email and a contract check with Julie Meyers. A rule that rolls the last deal forward automatically, or a regular exception report, could replace this.

leads.work: Approvals to write off old Strangers Gas volumes to Unaccounted for Gas: Clem Cernosek sends one form per meter, which Daren has to print, sign and return as a paper original
leads.why: Many near-identical template emails about volumes from 1999-2000, some under 30 MMBtu. Each needs a hand-signed paper copy. A batch approval or a threshold rule could replace this.

leads.work: Enerfin/TETCO meter 98-0439 reconciliation: deals between HPL, ENA and Dynegy extended by small amounts, retroactive nominations, and volumes changed again and again because the two sides' allocations differ
leads.why: Long threads involving many people over tiny volumes (9-141 dec). Victor says 'We go round and round at this point changing volumes two, three or more times' and that Enerfin's numbers change often. The OBA start date was changed without anyone being told.

leads.work: Moving ECC (Enron Canada) deals out of US books into the FT-US/CAND-ERMS book: Stacey Vallejo sends requests deal by deal, and Darron forwards each one on to his book administrators
leads.why: Repeated requests from November to December. Invoicing for ECC and ENA is held up until the deals are fixed. Darron forwarded the same request twice. A validation rule at deal booking could prevent the errors in the first place.

leads.work: Requests for P&L top sheets and curve shift reports for the auditors' (AA) monthly and quarterly gas testing: gathered by hand for each book and passed on by Darron
leads.why: Monthly requests from Sharon Smith and Carrie Richardson list books and top-5-day curve shift reports. Some items had to be chased up later because they were missing. This is a standard document package that could be produced automatically.

leads.work: Nightly book officialization, V@R position checks, post-id macro and verification sheet; flat books must still be officialized for credit
leads.why: Every book administrator checks their own positions each night and controllers get a verification sheet. Darron had to remind staff to run the macro every night. A book was officialized 4 times. Credit picks up the previous day's position if a book is not officialized.

leads.work: Price changes in Sitara for EnerVest S#27239, requested by email every month
leads.why: Tricia Truong asks for the rate to be changed every production month. The first request took weeks and several follow-ups. This could be set up as an index or formula price, or as a standing feed.

leads.work: Fixing duplicate Sitara deals and deal bridge failures between EOL, TAGG and Sitara
leads.why: The bridge failed, deals were double-booked, and they had to be killed by hand across regions. The link field was not filled in. TDS positions were reloaded after an outage. Recurring system problems take staff time.

leads.work: Schedule C reserve notices emailed by hand to Chris Abel/Thibodeaux each time money is moved in or out
leads.why: Short one-line notices sent over and over ('We released $75M tonight'). This could be logged in a system or reported automatically.

leads.work: Daily Enovate DPR check: Darron confirms the open position and P&L to Falcone and Abel by email
leads.why: Draft DPRs are checked each day and confirmed by hand, which looks like a daily pattern.

leads.work: Setting up curves and books in ERMS, RisktRAC and TAGG, and getting access, through manual forms and email requests
leads.why: Shona's memo says procedures are not being followed and many ERMS curves are missing from RisktRAC, so a weekly check had to be added. There are also emails asking for access, printing rights and curves to be added to TAGG, and lists of book codes typed out by hand for others.

leads.work: Old pricing and volume disputes with counterparties and invoice research (HESCO, TXU Lone Star, Wyman Gordon, Samson, TGLO): prices missing from deal tickets, done months later
leads.why: Repeated back and forth to find prices and volumes for 1999-2000 production, plus underpayment claims (HESCO said $32K). Often caused by traders leaving or deals not being booked.

leads.work: Contract assignments and wrong counterparties on deals (Cannon to Kinder Morgan, HPLC vs ENA), with retro assignments moved by hand by volume management
leads.why: The retro assignment process means volume management moves months of volume by hand. Credit exposure stays open until the change is made. Schedulers cannot change counterparties themselves.

leads.work: Monthly plant and meter allocation calculations done by hand (CLECO meter 3527 minus 9662, Big Thicket shrink, King Ranch elections, Teco Indian Springs PVR)
leads.why: Netting and allocation between meters each month, done by people outside Enron and checked against worksheets. The CLECO email asks who will do the monthly allocation. Volumes are checked against worksheets by eye.

leads.work: Reorganizing HR and PEP supervisor records, plus cost-centre allocation percentages sent in each month
leads.why: Several emails were needed to correct who reports to whom in PEP. Allocation percentages are collected every month from many managers. A job survey and matching exercise is repeated each year.

leads.work: Basis position roll-off on the Benchmark not done for some traders, and month-end flash coordination
leads.why: Manual steps get missed ('I didn't remind Kevin'). The flash status is chased by email before the CPR file is built.

leads.work: Bad estimates in POPS and imbalance issues needing checks by hand
leads.why: Weekend numbers were copied from the day before, so staff are told to double check all numbers. This points to a data feed problem.

leads.work: Holiday staffing, PRC meetings and similar scheduling coordinated by reply-all email
leads.why: Many reply-all answers to one staffing request. These are minor, but they happen every year.

leads.work: Large volumes of personal joke email forwarded on company mail
leads.why: Dozens of forwards with attachments (exe, mpg, jpg) sent from work accounts. This costs time and carries security risk.
